sentences.text: This Criminal Petition is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioner-accused No.7 in CC No.810 of 2020 on the file of the Hon'ble I-Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Godavarikhani, registered for the offences under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 409 IPC.

entities.text: I-Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Godavarikhani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri Sridhar Lonkala, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri E. Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1-State and Sri K. Arvind Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for Central Government-respondent No.2.
2 ETD,J 3.

The case of the prosecution is that accused No.1 was working as UDC in the Coal Mines Provident Fund office (CMPF), situated at I.B. Colony, Godavari Khani and that the accused Nos.2 to 17 are the employees of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) and are the members in CMPF.

It is alleged that accused No.1 in collusion with accused Nos.2 to 17 has fraudulently tampered and manipulated the entries in the ledger cards of accused No.2 to A17 increasing the actual balance amount with an ulterior motive misappropriated and cheated the firm to a tune of Rs.20,22,000/-
and gained personal benefits.

Thus, the case has been investigated and charge sheet is filed against the accused for the offences under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 409 IPC.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the police have mechanically filed charge sheet without conducting any investigation and that all the allegations point out only against A1.
The petitioner herein is accused No.7, who is unconnected with the allegations and that no fraud can be alleged against the petitioner herein.

He further submitted that the acts if any committed by Vodanala Srinivas vs The State Of Telangana, And Another on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147042279/
1 accused No.1 cannot make petitioner-accused No.7 to be liable for any offence.

sentences.text: He further has submitted that the departmental proceedings were concluded against the accused No.1 and accused 3 ETD,J No.1 got exonerated in the case and thus no offence can be attributed to the petitioner herein.
He, therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioner.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2-de facto complainant has submitted that the petitioner herein is the beneficiary of the fraud committed by accused No.1 and that it came to the notice of the office of respondent No.2 when the auditing was done.
He further submitted that it is financial fraud committed against the company, which cannot be excused and that they have ample material to prove the offence against the petitioner herein.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. Perused the record.
7.

It is alleged that accused No.1 has committed a financial fraud against the SCCL by tampering with the entries in the ledger cards of several employees of SCCL and the petitioner herein is one of such employees.
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner has not committed any fraud and therefore, he cannot be prosecuted.
However, it is pertinent to take note of the fact that the petitioner is the alleged beneficiary of the fraud committed by accused No.1.
The criminal element of forging 4 ETD,J the entries in the ledger cards of the employees is alleged.
Though the counsel for the petitioner contends that accused No.1 is exonerated in the departmental proceedings, the finding of departmental proceedings cannot have any bearing on this petition.
The statements of witnesses point out the alleged offences.
LWs.2 to 4 are the employees of CMPF office.
Their evidence is crucial, which needs to be examined during the course of trial.
The veracity of these witnesses and the documentary evidence produced by them have to be tested during the course of trial to bring the truth or otherwise in the allegations against the petitioner.
Hence, it is not a fit case to quash the proceedings against the petitioner at this stage.
However, it is deemed appropriate to dispose of the petition by dispensing with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial court.

8. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of dispensing with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial court provided he is represented by a counsel before the trial court on every date of hearing and shall appear before the trial court as and when his presence is required.
